rav.text: Vraska takes control of the Golgari and becomes a voice for gorgons.
After Jarad's death she moves the Golgari court back into Svogthos and builds a throne of petrified opponents.
Bolas's plan nears fruition as Vraska, Domri and Ral fall under his sway, and at his orders Vraska petrifies and kills Isperia.

When Aurelia tries to arrest Ral, Kaya and Vraska, Vraska challenges and assassinates her; in the New Phyrexian Invasion, a compleated Vraska leads the compleated Golgari to the surface, targeting the Azorius.

xln.text: Vraska is a pirate captain on the high seas of Ixalan when Nicol Bolas hires her, reads her mind and offers to make her Guildmaster of the Golgari if she retrieves an item from the Golden City of Orazca, and she accepts, and Bolas gives her the thaumatic compass along with a spell to call his associate and the knowledge of sailing.

When her crew spots a castaway, she recognizes Jace Beleren and means to petrify him, but she sees how ill he is, drops her gaze and learns he remembers nothing, so she spares him and lets him stay aboard.

Jace is amazed rather than afraid when she turns a vampire captain to stone, and he accepts her invitation to join the crew; as they talk, she tells him about Ravnica and the Azorius arrests that put her in prison, and each realizes neither wants to hurt the other.

A storm and a Legion of Dusk ship converge, The Belligerent rams into the rocks, and Vraska shows Jace that they are both planeswalkers, and racing the other factions to Orazca, she decides Jace is someone she can trust, petrifies Huatli's clawfoot and retakes the stolen compass, and at Orazca she and Jace meet Azor, and Vraska uses Bolas's spell so that Tezzeret seizes the Immortal Sun through a planar portal.
Jace's memories return and he forgives her, and she has him remove her memories of him so Bolas cannot read them.

rix.text: Vraska realizes that Jace's injury has left his mind unable to hold his memories, and she sees them in bursts, among them a teenage Jace being tattooed and the sphinx Alhammarret on a rooftop.
She holds the weeping Jace, the first time in years she has touched anyone willingly, and apologizes for trying to kill him on Ravnica; Jace forgives her.

When Azor reveals that the Immortal Sun is the lock of his prison, Vraska realizes it is what traps planeswalkers, and she and Jace deduce that Bolas has made an army he can transport and wants her help to unleash it on Ravnica.
She and Jace plan to betray Bolas by accepting his offer, and she asks Jace to take and hide her memories of him; he seals them in a warded box in her mind.

Vraska casts the spell that opens a portal beneath the Immortal Sun, which is pulled to another plane, and she planeswalks away; on the meditation plane Bolas scours her memories, accepts her account and rewards her with a kingdom and the location of Jarad.

grn.text: Vraska's story on Ravnica begins with the Azorius Senate's mass arrest of Golgari, in which she is imprisoned and beaten near death, and her planeswalker spark ignites and throws her to another plane.

She returns to Ravnica and begins her vengeful assassinations, and after Nicol Bolas rewards her with the location where Jarad is imprisoned, she frees and kills Jarad and establishes herself as Golgari guildmaster.
The Erstwhile become a ready-made army for her and the kraul become valued forces of the Swarm.

She leads Golgari forces into Orzhova as a distraction so Kaya can kill the Obzedat, but Bolas forces her to choose and she betrays Ral Zarek and Kaya, which leads to Hekara's death at the hands of a possessed Lavinia.
After the guild summit she kills Isperia, fulfilling Bolas's demands and her personal revenge, and the cooperation of the guilds collapses.

war.text: Vraska kills Isperia in a fit of rage at the guild summit, breaking down negotiations and making Dovin the Azorius guildmaster, and then flees to Ixalan.
When Bolas offers her leadership over the Golgari if she finds the Immortal Sun, she and Jace reach the Meditation Plane, where she tries to hold Jace back as Elspeth attacks Bolas.
She planeswalks in to claim her throne, the Golgari leaders bow to her without challenge, and she pledges the Golgari to the fight against Bolas.
Kaya and Zarek accept her offer of help, and she turns three pursuing Eternals to stone to seal the hole behind the last evacuees.

Vraska senses that the Immortal Sun has been shut down, and she and Jace reunite and agree to try a relationship after Bolas is dead or they are. Afterward the guilds assign her to hunt Dovin Baan, and she finds him and plots with him to fake his death in a staged fight.

mh1.text: Vraska appears on this set's cards as a planeswalker who speaks of the rise of the downtrodden.

mom.text: Vraska is compleated, her throat and tendrils turning to metal, and her self retreats into a hidden corner of her mind as she is overwhelmed.

As a general for Elesh Norn she rides a Realmbreaker branch down over Ravnica, has it plunge through the Azorius Senate, and has Phyrexian agents blind the guards she finds at the prison where she was once held, and she leads the Phyrexians into the Golgari undercity, transforming her people while Realmbreaker upends Korozda and cracks Svogthos, and her forces destroy the roof of the Chamber of the Guildpact.
Ral Zarek fights through the Phyrexian ranks and disables her with a device attuned to Phyrexian oil, and her forces abandon her broken body.

Lying half-flesh and half-metal beneath the rubble, she meets Jace in her mind, and he forgives her and tells her the part that led the invasion was not her; they share a kiss and he tells her he loves her too.

Jace spirits her away to Vryn, where Ranna burns most of the oil from her and cures her, but Vraska realizes she has lost her planeswalker spark, and she later recruits Malcolm and Breeches on Ixalan for Jace's plan, and she and Jace seize Loot during the Vault Heist.

otj.text: Vraska appears at Oko's side, to the stunned surprise of Ral Zarek, and Oko decides Kellan should join them over her objection, and she tells the crew that the man who can read their artifact is on a train to Prosperity, and then goes into Tarnation disguised as a Hellspur, where she turns one to stone in a saloon brawl before the crew is captured.

When Tinybones frees them, Vraska petrifies the guarding Hellspurs, and Oko admits that he planned the capture all along, and once the ward breaks she descends with Oko, and when Ral confronts her she says the only way to fix what she has done is to get what is inside the vault.

After Oko opens the vault she petrifies him, saying his services are no longer required, and Oko planeswalks away before the stone reaches his head; by the time Kellan reaches Annie, Vraska, Jace and the child have vanished.

Jace finds Vraska wounded and compleated on a rooftop, reverses her phyresis, and carries her to his mother Ranna on Vryn, where Vraska asks that Jace be saved first, and healed with a phoenix feather, Vraska discovers she can no longer planeswalk, and she and Jace decide the Multiverse is too broken to fix and settle on rebirth.
They reunite with the prize from the vault, a child named Loot whose mind holds a map of the whole Multiverse, and promise to protect him as their ward.

fra.text: Vraska's whole world falls apart when Chandra and Ajani tell her that Jace is alive, and she agrees to help reach him, carrying a wrapped package from Ranna, and in a dream, General Beleren tells her he can be both a good man and a monster, and she wakes realizing that Jace is both.
With Garruk, Ajani and Chandra she exposes a false Liliana and punches her unconscious, then loses time and memory in a looping tower.

Facing the Theorist, she asks him to stop and tells him he is a killer who will murder billions, but he wipes her memory and sends them out again and again, finally commanding them to fight each other and leaving only the knowledge that he cannot be defeated, so Vraska concludes they have only fought what is left of Jace, and Tam tells her the Theorist can only be beaten by a telepath.

She refuses to give up when the Theorist asks, and he throws the group into a portal, where they meet the Detective, an aberration of Jace; Vraska embraces him, saying we are who we choose to be, and kisses him when he says he chooses to kill his own ambition.

Vraska realizes that for the spell to slow, Jace's body must die, and though she objects, the Detective asks the others to find the rest of him and hold the parts in their minds, and she takes in the Nihilist, promising it is her turn to save him, but on a rooftop memory in the rain, compelled by the sphinx, she steps off the edge of the building.
